title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 2a: ranking designs by the full DFN model stopped at cycle 10 matches 100-cycle DFN at Spearman 0.977 against 0.834 for a full 100-cycle SPMe run, at the same wall time (4.0 s against 4.1 s), and its top 5 contain the best design; milestone 1: SPMe's own minimum electrolyte concentration flags the designs it mis-scores (ROC AUC 0.997, 7 of 49) (modelled, PyBaMM OKane2022, stack level)
summary: A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 2a treats the cycle count as a fidelity axis on the 49 designs of energy-cell-dfn: ranking by DFN's score at cycle 10 agrees with the 100-cycle DFN ranking at Spearman 0.977, against 0.834 for a full 100-cycle SPMe run (paired bootstrap difference 0.138, 95% 0.057–0.271), at equal median wall time (4.0 s against 4.1 s); the top 5 by 10-cycle DFN contain the DFN best, the top 5 by SPMe miss it by 2.1 Wh/kg, and even 2-cycle DFN (0.915, 1.4 s) beats every SPM and SPMe rung. SPMe's agreement falls as the horizon grows, and a linear fade extrapolation fails (Spearman 0.01). Milestone 1: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration classifies the 7 designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 (bootstrap 95% 0.980–1.000). Re-runs reproduce the committed SPMe and DFN scores exactly. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, a stratified 49-design sample, serial timings from one 4-core machine, no measured cell for these designs.
